title: The boot cover's network wait no longer removes fetch/XHR wrappers other plugins installed after it
expect: 'a wrapper another plugin installed after it survives the restore' passes: after networkSettles resolves, scope.fetch is still the later wrapper and a call through it reaches the real fetch.
'it puts fetch back the way it found it' still passes: with no later wrapper, fetch is restored to the original.
evidence: tasks/evidence/passwords-mount-followups/README.md — on tracy-srd 09/10 a window.fetch setter trap showed @tracy/dsh-brand's finish() assigning back the fetch it saved, dropping dsh-passwords' picker wrapper installed after it (the owner's delete-folder button never attached, even at the root).
fence: network-settles.mjs finish(): restores fetch / XHR open / send only while they are still its own wrapper; a wrapper left under someone else's becomes a pass-through.

tests: a wrapper another plugin installed after it survives the restore
it puts fetch back the way it found it
